title: While & When

vocab.ex: While I was cooking, the phone rang.
I was sleeping when you called.
As I was leaving, it started to rain.
During the meeting, my phone rang.
At the moment, I was driving home.
Just then, the lights went out.
Right when I sat down, my boss called.
All of a sudden, the music stopped.
In the meantime, she was preparing dinner.
Meanwhile, he was waiting outside.
The background action was longer than the interruption.
The interrupting action is usually shorter.
I was in a traffic jam when she called.
Someone was knocking while I cooked.
Use a comma when "while" starts the sentence.
The sequence of events matters in a story.
The phone call interrupted our dinner.
We continued talking despite the noise.
I noticed she was upset while we talked.
She realized her mistake while driving.
Simultaneous actions both use Past Continuous.
Use when + Past Simple for one moment.
While she cooked, he was cleaning — two ongoing actions.
Unexpectedly, the train stopped.
At exactly that time, the alarm rang.
Both events happened at once.

vocab.en: to be in the middle of
vocab.ex: I was in the middle of dinner when she arrived.
The noise disturbed my concentration.
A sudden noise woke everyone up.
The rain started without warning.

grammar.title: While & When: conectando duas ações no passado
rules: WHILE + Past Continuous (ação longa, de fundo): "While I was cooking..."
WHEN + Past Simple (ação curta, que interrompe): "...the phone rang."
Se a frase com WHILE vem primeiro, use vírgula: "While I was cooking, the phone rang."
Também é possível usar WHEN com Past Continuous para duas ações simultâneas: "When I arrived, she was leaving."

rows: As I was leaving, it rained.
